nodes.title: Analyzing and contrasting linear relationships using rate of change (slope) and start value (y-intercept).

nodes.label: Interpreting the Point of Intersection in Real-World Context
nodes.title: Explaining the intersection as the point where two quantities are equal or conditions balance in a given context.

nodes.title: Translating contextual information into a linear model by identifying the rate of change and initial value.

nodes.title: Determining the constant rate of change from differences in y over differences in x in tabular data.

nodes.title: Solve for a missing side in a right triangle by selecting and rearranging SOH-CAH-TOA given one acute angle and one side.

nodes.title: Determine an acute angle in a right triangle from given side lengths using arcsin, arccos, or arctan.

nodes.title: Model real-life scenarios as right triangles and use a^2 + b^2 = c^2 to find unknown heights or horizontal distances.

nodes.label: Sine Ratio in a Right Triangle
nodes.title: Use sinθ = opposite/hypotenuse to relate an acute angle to the ratio of two sides.

nodes.label: Cosine Ratio in a Right Triangle
nodes.title: Use cosθ = adjacent/hypotenuse to relate an acute angle to the ratio of two sides.

nodes.label: Tangent Ratio in a Right Triangle
nodes.title: Use tanθ = opposite/adjacent to relate an acute angle to the ratio of two sides.

nodes.label: Angles of Elevation and Depression
nodes.title: Interpret angles measured from the horizontal in real-world contexts to set up right triangle models.

nodes.label: Identifying Opposite, Adjacent, and Hypotenuse in Right Triangles
nodes.title: Determine side names relative to a reference acute angle to correctly choose a trig ratio.

nodes.label: Right Triangle Modelling from Word Problems
nodes.title: Translate context about heights, distances, and angles into a labeled right-triangle diagram before computation.

nodes.label: Dilation (Enlargement) with Center and Scale Factor
nodes.title: A similarity transformation mapping each point to a new point along the ray from a fixed center, with distance multiplied by scale factor k.

nodes.label: Area Scaling under Dilation
nodes.title: Under a dilation with scale factor k, areas of plane figures are multiplied by k^2.

nodes.label: Centre of Enlargement
nodes.title: The fixed point from which all distances are scaled and directions preserved in a dilation.
nodes.broader_concept: Dilation (Enlargement) with Center and Scale Factor

nodes.label: Scale Factor in Dilation
nodes.title: The ratio k determining size change in a dilation; k>1 enlarges, 0<k<1 reduces; commonly taken as rational in school tasks.
nodes.broader_concept: Dilation (Enlargement) with Center and Scale Factor

nodes.title: Producing the image of a polygon given a center and scale factor by extending rays from the center through vertices and scaling lengths by k.

nodes.label: Reflection in a Line (Axial Symmetry)
nodes.title: An isometry mapping each point to its mirror image across a given line, which is the perpendicular bisector of each segment joining a point to its image.

nodes.label: Rotation about a Point
nodes.title: An isometry turning a figure around a fixed center by a specified angle and direction.

nodes.label: Translation by a Vector
nodes.title: An isometry shifting every point of a figure by the same directed distance (vector).

nodes.label: Central Symmetry (Point Reflection)
nodes.title: An isometry mapping each point to the point opposite with respect to a center so that the center is the midpoint of each preimage–image segment.

nodes.label: Identifying Axes of Symmetry in 2D Shapes
nodes.title: Locating all lines of symmetry in simple plane figures such as polygons and common shapes.

nodes.label: Deductive Reasoning in Geometry
nodes.title: Using logical inference from axioms and proven results to justify geometric claims.

nodes.label: Proof
nodes.title: A logically coherent argument that establishes the truth of a mathematical statement.

nodes.label: Theorem
nodes.title: A mathematical statement proven true based on axioms and previously established results.

nodes.label: Axiom
nodes.title: A fundamental assumption accepted without proof, used as a starting point for deductions.

nodes.label: Corollary
nodes.title: A proposition that follows directly from a theorem with little or no additional proof.

nodes.label: Logical Implication (implies)
nodes.title: Using p ⇒ q to express that one statement logically leads to another.

nodes.label: Converse of a Statement
nodes.title: Forming q ⇒ p from an implication p ⇒ q and analyzing its truth independently of the original statement.

nodes.label: Biconditional (if and only if)
nodes.title: Using p ⇔ q to state that each condition is both necessary and sufficient for the other.

nodes.label: Logical Equivalence (is equivalent to)
nodes.title: Recognizing when two statements always share the same truth value and denoting this with ⇔ or ≡.

nodes.label: Proof by Contradiction
nodes.title: Establishing a statement by assuming its negation and deriving a contradiction.

nodes.label: Pythagorean Theorem
nodes.title: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.

nodes.label: Slope of a Line
nodes.title: The rate of change of y with respect to x; computed from two points or from y = mx + c.

nodes.label: Parallel Lines via Equal Slopes
nodes.title: Two non-vertical lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are equal.

nodes.label: Perpendicular Lines via Negative Reciprocal Slopes
nodes.title: Two lines are perpendicular if their slopes are negative reciprocals, equivalently m1*m2 = -1 when defined.

nodes.label: General Form of a Linear Equation (ax + by + c = 0)
nodes.title: Recognizing and using ax + by + c = 0 as the equation of a straight line in the plane.

nodes.label: Angle Between Two Lines from Slopes
nodes.title: Computing the angle between lines with slopes m1 and m2 using tan(theta) = |(m1 - m2)/(1 + m1*m2)|.

nodes.label: Perpendicular Distance from a Point to a Line
nodes.title: Using d = |A*x0 + B*y0 + C| / sqrt(A^2 + B^2) for the line A x + B y + C = 0.

nodes.label: Internal Division of a Line Segment (Section Formula)
nodes.title: Finding the point that divides a segment in ratio m:n internally: ((m*x2 + n*x1)/(m+n), (m*y2 + n*y1)/(m+n)).

nodes.label: Circle Equation in Center-Radius Form
nodes.title: (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 represents a circle with center (h, k) and radius r.

nodes.label: Circle Equation in General Form and Parameter Extraction
nodes.title: For x^2 + y^2 + 2g x + 2f y + c = 0, the center is (-g, -f) and the radius is r = sqrt(g^2 + f^2 - c).

nodes.label: Intersection of a Line and a Circle
nodes.title: Solving a linear-quadratic system to find intersection points; the discriminant determines 0, 1, or 2 solutions.

nodes.label: Area of a Triangle from Coordinates
nodes.title: Using Area = 1/2 * |x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)| for vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x3, y3).

nodes.label: Definition of Sine for All Real Angles
nodes.title: Define sin θ for any real θ using the unit circle, including signs by quadrant and periodicity.

nodes.label: Definition of Cosine for All Real Angles
nodes.title: Define cos θ for any real θ using the unit circle, including signs by quadrant and periodicity.

nodes.label: Definition of Tangent for All Real Angles
nodes.title: Define tan θ as sin θ / cos θ with domain restrictions where cos θ ≠ 0, including period π.

nodes.label: Radian Measure of Angles
nodes.title: Measure angles in radians; relate arc length s = rθ and convert between degrees and radians.

nodes.label: Graph of the Sine Function
nodes.title: Plot y = sin θ, identifying amplitude 1, period 2π, phase, and key points and intercepts.

nodes.label: Graph of the Cosine Function
nodes.title: Plot y = cos θ, identifying amplitude 1, period 2π, phase, and key points and intercepts.

nodes.label: Graph of the Tangent Function
nodes.title: Plot y = tan θ, showing period π and vertical asymptotes at odd multiples of π/2.

nodes.label: Graphing y = a + b sin(cθ)
nodes.title: Graph sine functions with vertical shift a, amplitude |b|, and period 2π/|c|.

nodes.label: Graphing y = a + b cos(cθ)
nodes.title: Graph cosine functions with vertical shift a, amplitude |b|, and period 2π/|c|.

nodes.label: Solving Trigonometric Equations with Multiple-Angle Arguments
nodes.title: Find all solutions to equations like sin(nθ)=0 or cos(nθ)=1/2 using reference angles and periodicity.

nodes.label: Law of Sines (2D)
nodes.title: Use the sine rule a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C to solve non-right triangles.

nodes.label: Law of Cosines (2D)
nodes.title: Use the cosine rule c^2 = a^2 + b^2 − 2ab cos C to solve non-right triangles.

nodes.label: Area of a Triangle Using Trigonometry
nodes.title: Compute triangle area with A = 1/2 ab sin C when two sides and the included angle are known.

nodes.label: Applying Pythagoras' Theorem in 2D
nodes.title: Use a^2 + b^2 = c^2 to find unknown side lengths in right triangles and solve 2D problems.

nodes.label: Trigonometry in 3D Problem Solving
nodes.title: Apply right-triangle trigonometry and triangle laws to three-dimensional contexts, including line-of-sight and distances.

nodes.label: Arc Length of a Circle
nodes.title: Calculate arc length using s = rθ for θ in radians.

nodes.label: Area of a Sector of a Circle
nodes.title: Calculate sector area using A = 1/2 r^2 θ for θ in radians.

nodes.label: Trigonometric Ratios in Surd Form
nodes.title: Express exact values of sine, cosine, and tangent for special angles (e.g., 30°, 45°, 60°) using surds.

nodes.label: Enlargement (Dilation) with Given Centre and Scale Factor
nodes.title: A similarity transformation about a fixed centre that maps each point along the ray from the centre, multiplying its distance from the centre by a positive scale factor k.

nodes.label: Area Scaling Under Enlargement
nodes.title: Under an enlargement with scale factor k, the area of any planar figure is multiplied by k^2.

nodes.label: Scale Factor of Enlargement (Positive Rational k)
nodes.title: The ratio k by which all distances from the centre are multiplied during enlargement, restricted here to k ∈ Q with k > 0.

nodes.label: Finding the Image Under Enlargement
nodes.title: Given a centre and scale factor k, compute or construct the image of a point or shape by scaling distances from the centre by k along the corresponding rays.

nodes.label: Determining the Scale Factor from Preimage and Image
nodes.title: Calculate k by comparing corresponding lengths or distances from the centre between a figure and its image.

nodes.label: Classifying Enlargements as Reductions or Magnifications
nodes.title: Identify whether an enlargement shrinks a figure (0 < k < 1) or enlarges it (k > 1).

nodes.label: Rational Numbers (Q)
nodes.title: Numbers that can be expressed as a quotient of two integers with nonzero denominator; include terminating and repeating decimals and percentages.

nodes.label: Converting Between Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
nodes.title: Translate a rational number among fraction, decimal, and percent forms to show their equivalence.

nodes.label: Terminating and Repeating Decimals as Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Identify that decimals that end or repeat represent rational numbers and convert them to fractions.

nodes.label: Addition of Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Compute sums of rational numbers, including fractions and decimals, using common denominators or place value.

nodes.label: Subtraction of Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Compute differences of rational numbers by adding the additive inverse or aligning place value/denominators.

nodes.label: Multiplication of Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Multiply rational numbers using fraction multiplication or decimal place-value methods and interpret scaling.

nodes.label: Division of Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Divide rational numbers by multiplying by the reciprocal (for nonzero divisors) or using decimal algorithms.

nodes.label: Integers (Z)
nodes.title: The set of whole numbers and their opposites, including zero.

nodes.label: Addition of Integers (Signed Numbers)
nodes.title: Add positive and negative integers using opposites, absolute value, and vector/number line models.

nodes.label: Subtraction of Integers (Signed Numbers)
nodes.title: Subtract integers by adding the additive inverse and interpret differences on a number line.

nodes.label: Multiplication of Integers (Signed Numbers)
nodes.title: Multiply integers using sign rules derived from properties and patterns (positive×negative, etc.).

nodes.label: Division of Integers (Signed Numbers)
nodes.title: Divide integers using sign rules consistent with multiplication and quotients.

nodes.label: Natural Numbers (N)
nodes.title: The set of counting numbers starting at 1 (1, 2, 3, ...).

nodes.label: Decomposition Strategy for Addition and Subtraction
nodes.title: Break numbers into place-value parts to simplify addition and subtraction in whole numbers.

nodes.label: Skip Counting as a Model for Multiplication
nodes.title: Use repeated counting by equal intervals to represent and compute multiplication facts.

nodes.label: Array Model of Multiplication
nodes.title: Represent multiplication as rows and columns to visualize equal groups and area.

nodes.label: Equal Groups Model for Multiplication and Division
nodes.title: Interpret multiplication as combining equal groups and division as partitioning or measuring equal groups.

nodes.label: Ordering Rational Numbers on the Number Line
nodes.title: Place and compare rational numbers on a number line using value and common benchmarks.

nodes.label: Number Line Model for Integer Addition and Subtraction
nodes.title: Use directed moves on a number line to model addition and subtraction with integers.

nodes.label: Inverse Relationship Between Addition and Subtraction
nodes.title: Recognize subtraction as adding the additive inverse and use this relationship to solve problems.

nodes.label: Inverse Relationship Between Multiplication and Division
nodes.title: Understand division as the inverse of multiplication and apply to fact families and equations.

nodes.label: Commutative Property of Addition and Multiplication
nodes.title: Changing the order of addends or factors does not change the sum or product.

nodes.label: Associative Property of Addition and Multiplication
nodes.title: Changing the grouping of addends or factors does not change the sum or product.

nodes.label: Distributive Property of Multiplication over Addition
nodes.title: Multiply a sum by distributing the factor across addends (a(b+c)=ab+ac) and use for computation.

nodes.label: Order of Operations with Brackets
nodes.title: Evaluate numerical expressions using agreed order (parentheses, exponents if present, multiplication/division, addition/subtraction).

nodes.label: Interpreting Negative Numbers in Real-World Contexts
nodes.title: Model and interpret negative quantities such as debts or temperatures below zero.

nodes.label: Finding a Fraction of a Quantity
nodes.title: Calculate a part of a whole by multiplying a fraction by a whole number amount in context.

nodes.label: Reciprocal of a Nonzero Rational Number
nodes.title: Identify the multiplicative inverse of a nonzero rational number and use it to perform division.

nodes.label: Irrational Numbers: Definition and Recognition
nodes.title: Identify real numbers that cannot be expressed as a ratio of integers, e.g., non-terminating, non-repeating decimals like √2 and π.

nodes.label: Real vs Rational Numbers Distinction (R ≠ Q)
nodes.title: Understand that the set of real numbers strictly contains the rationals, implying the existence of irrational numbers.

nodes.label: Complex Numbers in Rectangular Form (a+ib)
nodes.title: Represent complex numbers as a+ib with real and imaginary parts, enabling algebraic operations.

nodes.label: Arithmetic of Complex Numbers in Rectangular Form
nodes.title: Perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division with complex numbers using a+ib and conjugates.

nodes.label: Argand Diagram: Plotting Complex Numbers
nodes.title: Plot complex numbers on the complex plane with real axis horizontal and imaginary axis vertical.

nodes.label: Modulus of a Complex Number as Distance
nodes.title: Interpret |a+ib| = √(a²+b²) as the distance from the origin in the Argand plane.

nodes.label: Complex Conjugate and Its Properties
nodes.title: Use conjugation z↦z̄ with z̄=a−ib; know that (z+w)̄=z̄+w̄ and (zw)̄=z̄w̄, and zz̄=|z|².

nodes.label: Representing Real Numbers on the Number Line
nodes.title: Locate natural, integer, rational, and irrational numbers on a continuous number line.

nodes.label: Scientific Notation (a×10^n) Representation
nodes.title: Express non-zero positive rational numbers as a×10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10 and n ∈ ℤ.

nodes.label: Arithmetic with Scientific Notation
nodes.title: Perform multiplication, division, addition, and subtraction on numbers in a×10^n form with exponent adjustments.

nodes.label: Prime Factorization of Natural Numbers
nodes.title: Express natural numbers uniquely (up to order) as a product of prime powers.

nodes.label: Factors and Multiples in Natural Numbers
nodes.title: Determine all divisors and multiples of a natural number and use divisibility properties.

nodes.label: Prime Numbers: Identification and Properties
nodes.title: Recognize primes and apply basic properties including tests of divisibility and primality in N.

nodes.label: Decimals as Equivalent Fractions
nodes.title: Convert terminating and recurring decimals to fractions by using place value or geometric series.

nodes.label: Geometric Construction of √2
nodes.title: Construct √2 using compass and straightedge, e.g., as the diagonal of a unit square.

nodes.label: Geometric Construction of √3
nodes.title: Construct √3 via 30-60-90 triangle or using an equilateral triangle of side 1.

nodes.label: Proof that √2 is Irrational
nodes.title: Show √2 ∉ ℚ using proof by contradiction (parity argument) or infinite descent.

nodes.label: Mathematical Induction
nodes.title: Prove statements indexed by natural numbers using base case and inductive step.

nodes.label: Inductive Proof: Sum of First n Natural Numbers
nodes.title: Prove 1+2+…+n = n(n+1)/2 using induction.

nodes.label: Inductive Proof: Sum of a Finite Geometric Series
nodes.title: Prove S_n = a(1−r^n)/(1−r) for r≠1 by induction.

nodes.label: Bernoulli’s Inequality
nodes.title: Show (1+x)^n ≥ 1+nx for x > −1 and n ∈ ℕ, e.g., by induction.

nodes.label: Inductive Inequality: 2^n ≥ n^2 (n ≥ 4)
nodes.title: Use induction to prove exponential growth dominates quadratic for n≥4.

nodes.label: Divisibility Result: 3 divides 4^n − 1
nodes.title: Prove 3|(4^n−1) for all n∈ℕ using induction or modular arithmetic.

nodes.label: Geometric Sequence: Definition and General Term
nodes.title: Define a_n = ar^{n−1} and identify the common ratio r.

nodes.label: Finite Geometric Series: Sum Formula
nodes.title: Use S_n = a(1−r^n)/(1−r) (r≠1) to compute sums.

nodes.label: Infinite Geometric Series: Sum to Infinity
nodes.title: For |r|<1, compute S_∞ = a/(1−r).

nodes.label: Sum to Infinity via Limit of Partial Sums
nodes.title: Derive S_∞ by taking the limit of S_n as n→∞ when |r|<1.

nodes.label: Algebra of Limits (Sums, Products, Quotients)
nodes.title: Apply limit laws for sum, product, and quotient when limits exist and denominators are nonzero.

nodes.label: Limit of 1/n as n→∞
nodes.title: Recognize that lim_{n→∞} 1/n = 0 by basic limit reasoning.

nodes.label: Limit of r^n for |r|<1
nodes.title: Know that lim_{n→∞} r^n = 0 when the common ratio satisfies |r|<1.

nodes.label: Recurring Decimals as Geometric Series
nodes.title: Model repeating decimals as infinite geometric series to convert them to exact fractions.

nodes.label: Mortgage Repayment Formula via Geometric Series
nodes.title: Derive the annuity payment formula using present value of a finite geometric series.

nodes.label: Integer Arithmetic in Z
nodes.title: Carry out addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division with integers, noting closure and non-closure under division.

nodes.label: Rational Number Arithmetic in Q
nodes.title: Perform the four operations on rational numbers using fraction rules and simplification.

nodes.label: Real Number Arithmetic in R
nodes.title: Apply arithmetic operations to real numbers, including surd manipulation where appropriate.

nodes.label: Equivalence of Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
nodes.title: Recognizing and converting between equivalent representations of the same proportion as a fraction, decimal, or percent.

nodes.label: Calculating Percentages
nodes.title: Finding a given percentage of a quantity and expressing one quantity as a percentage of another.

nodes.label: Proportion as Equality of Ratios
nodes.title: Understanding that a proportion states two ratios are equal and using this relationship to solve problems.

nodes.label: Comparing Proportions Using FDP Equivalence
nodes.title: Comparing ratios or parts of a whole by converting them to a common representation such as fraction, decimal, or percent.

nodes.label: Prime Number Identification
nodes.title: Determining whether a natural number greater than 1 has exactly two distinct factors, 1 and itself.

nodes.label: Finding Factors of a Natural Number
nodes.title: Listing all integers that divide a given natural number without remainder and identifying factor pairs.

nodes.label: Identifying Multiples and Common Multiples
nodes.title: Generating multiples of a number and finding common multiples of two or more numbers.

nodes.label: Scientific Notation for Positive Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Expressing non-zero positive rational numbers in the form a×10^n with 1≤a<10 and n an integer.

nodes.label: Equality as a Relationship Between Expressions
nodes.title: Interpreting the equals sign as stating that two expressions have the same value and applying properties of equality.

nodes.label: Rounding to a Specified Degree of Accuracy
nodes.title: Rounding numbers to a required number of decimal places or significant figures to present final answers.

nodes.label: Order-of-Magnitude Check of Results
nodes.title: Assessing whether an answer is reasonable by comparing its scale to an estimated order of magnitude using powers of ten.

nodes.label: Using Inverse Operations to Verify Solutions
nodes.title: Checking results by reversing operations to see if the original conditions are satisfied (working backwards).

nodes.label: Estimation and Approximation of Calculations
nodes.title: Making and justifying approximate calculations to obtain quick, reasonable results when exact answers are unnecessary.

nodes.label: Index Notation for Integer Powers
nodes.title: Representing repeated multiplication using exponents, interpreting a^n for natural numbers n.

nodes.label: Square of a Number
nodes.title: Calculating and interpreting a^2 as the product of a number with itself.

nodes.label: Cube of a Number
nodes.title: Calculating and interpreting a^3 as the product of a number with itself three times.

nodes.label: Square Root of a Number
nodes.title: Interpreting √a as the principal number whose square equals a (for a ≥ 0 in real numbers).

nodes.label: Reciprocal of a Number
nodes.title: Finding the multiplicative inverse of a nonzero number, 1/a.

nodes.label: Negative Exponent as Reciprocal
nodes.title: Interpreting a^-1 as 1/a (and, more generally, a^-n as 1/a^n for n ∈ N).

nodes.label: Fractional Exponent 1/2 as Square Root
nodes.title: Interpreting a^(1/2) as √a for a ≥ 0 in the real number system.

nodes.label: Convert Between Radical and Exponential Form
nodes.title: Rewriting expressions such as √a as a^(1/2) and vice versa.

nodes.label: Classifying Sequences as Arithmetic, Geometric, or Neither
nodes.title: Determine whether a sequence has a constant difference, a constant ratio, or neither based on its terms.

nodes.label: Nth Term of an Arithmetic Sequence
nodes.title: Find and use the explicit formula a_n = a_1 + (n−1)d to describe the nth term of an arithmetic sequence.

nodes.label: Nth Term of a Geometric Sequence
nodes.title: Find and use the explicit formula a_n = a_1 r^(n−1) to describe the nth term of a geometric sequence.

nodes.label: Sum of First n Terms of an Arithmetic Series
nodes.title: Calculate S_n using S_n = n/2 (2a + (n−1)d) or S_n = n/2 (a + l) for an arithmetic series.

nodes.label: Finding the Common Difference of an Arithmetic Sequence
nodes.title: Compute the constant difference d by subtracting consecutive terms in an arithmetic sequence.

nodes.label: Finding the Common Ratio of a Geometric Sequence
nodes.title: Compute the constant ratio r by dividing consecutive terms in a geometric sequence.

nodes.label: Extending a Sequence from a Given Rule
nodes.title: Continue a sequence by applying its explicit or recursive rule to generate subsequent terms.

nodes.label: Generating a Sequence from a Recursive Rule
nodes.title: Use a recurrence relation to produce successive terms of a sequence from initial values.

nodes.label: Generalising Patterns into Algebraic Form
nodes.title: Express observed numeric patterns using variables and formulas, such as deriving an nth term expression.

nodes.label: Product of Powers with Same Base
nodes.title: a^p · a^q = a^(p+q) for the same nonzero base a.

nodes.label: Quotient of Powers with Same Base
nodes.title: a^p / a^q = a^(p−q) for a ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Power of a Power Rule
nodes.title: (a^p)^q = a^(pq).

nodes.label: Negative Exponent Rule
nodes.title: For a ≠ 0, a^(−p) = 1/a^p.

nodes.label: Power of a Product Rule
nodes.title: (ab)^p = a^p b^p.

nodes.label: Power of a Quotient Rule
nodes.title: (a/b)^p = a^p / b^p for b ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Fractional Exponents as Roots
nodes.title: For a > 0 and integer q > 0, a^(1/q) equals the qth root of a.

nodes.label: Rational Exponents Equivalence
nodes.title: For a > 0 and integers p, q with q > 0, a^(p/q) = (qth root of a)^p = qth root of (a^p).

nodes.label: Logarithm Product Rule
nodes.title: log_a(xy) = log_a x + log_a y for a > 0, a ≠ 1.

nodes.label: Logarithm Quotient Rule
nodes.title: log_a(x/y) = log_a x − log_a y for a > 0, a ≠ 1.

nodes.label: Logarithm Power Rule
nodes.title: log_a(x^q) = q log_a x for a > 0, a ≠ 1.

nodes.label: Change of Base Formula for Logarithms
nodes.title: log_a x = (log_b x) / (log_b a) for valid bases a, b.

nodes.label: Logarithm of Base Equals One
nodes.title: log_a a = 1 for a > 0, a ≠ 1.

nodes.label: Logarithm of One Equals Zero
nodes.title: log_a 1 = 0 for a > 0, a ≠ 1.

nodes.label: Sum to n Terms of an Arithmetic Series
nodes.title: Calculate the sum of the first n terms using S_n = n/2 [2a + (n−1)d] or S_n = n/2 (first term + last term).
